market_question: Will the Republicans win the Maine Senate race in 2026?
reasoning: Susan Collins is a moderate Republican incumbent with a proven ability to outperform the top of the ticket (won by 8.6 pp in 2020 while Trump lost Maine by 9 pp). Markets may be over-weighting her retirement risk; even if she retires, open-seat odds are not zero. My best estimate, given a ~60‑70 % chance she runs and decent win probabilities in either scenario, places Republican victory around 42 %, well above the 22.5 % implied.
evidence_points: Collins defeated Sara Gideon by 8.6 pp in 2020 while Biden won Maine by 9 pp, demonstrating strong crossover appeal.
She has not announced retirement; many senators serve into their late 70s, and no public signal indicates she will step down.
In an open seat, Maine’s current Democratic trend still gives a generic Republican a ~20‑25 % chance, so worst-case scenario still adds meaningful probability.
sources_consulted: David J. Wasserman / Cook Political Report early race analysis
